title: Level Editors
author: matt_williamson
selftext:
I hate designing levels in code. I've used Tiled in the past but it doesn't always fit the game I'm working on.

What I really enjoyed discovering is having the AI build a level editor into my games. With a proper app design, the feature is almost free.

I don't see it discussed. How many other are doing this. Are there better ways?

comments.author: gebuswon
comments.body: What sort of games are you making and what are the editors like?

replies.author: matt_williamson
replies.body: I made a Pull The Pin like game. The editor for that is just a basic tool bar for selecting and dropping objects. Then rotate, scale, and move. Level preview then export to JSON. The game didn't add anything to the genre so it is on the shelf.

comments.author: lucianw
comments.body:
My browser game has a declarative text file format for its levels. (it's a text heavy game).

I had codex build a live editor next to the game window, with normal code-editor like features (go-to-def, hover, find-references, syntax highlighting, lints). And it made it live, so that as I change stuff in the text editor then the game window changes instantly.

comments.author: Ferniclestix
comments.body:
I am, mines a top down arcade space rogue like,  the actual editor uses a combination of splines, polygonal shapes and a few other things to create terrain,  my nodes can be used to create radius based areas to spawn things.  ive got paths I can apply to say a ship with triggers and nodes attached allowing me to easily create dialogs, scripted sequences and dynamic encounters because I can create nested node graphs too so i can bring in a scripted sequence on the fly.

I built mine from the ground up, I built the editor first, my game does not even have its first level yet because I am focusing on teh tools. I want other users to be able to create maps, ships , weapons, effects, enemies, scripted sequences everything.

https://i.redd.it/f9m7nwhg250i1.gif

basically its an engine before its a game.   it also means much of the game itself will be made by me while it runs on an engine made by the AI.

in my opinion node graphs are the best way for some people to access things like programming because its not just a wall of unexplainable text.  but ive seen other methods too, the point is to be modular and have specific inputs and outputs so that things can be connected together in sensible ways that don't break things.

if its just a thing you are going to use, it could be as ugly as you want it.  i like my stuff pretty regardless lol.

replies.author: clydeagain
replies.body: I'm very interested in this, can you have claude write something up on how this can be remade for others' project?

replies.author: Ferniclestix
replies.body:
unfortunately this isn't a one prompt type deal, this is a 4 month long project so far with me prompting individual changes.  there are so many ways for claude to break this because it works in ways that are i guess you could say are unique or at least non standard which is where claude starts kinda doing its own thing.  
I built these on a system by system basis. I understand the underlying logic of the system and had to individually tell it how to do things like how to treat wires in my node graph, how to pass information through, how to use it . what each wire has.  its kinda complex lol.  

  
heres a look at some of my change log for an idea.

\# Changelog



Format: \`\[YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM UTC\] file1.py, file2.py :: what changed\`

Chronological, oldest at top, new entries appended at the bottom. Append-only — don't rewrite old entries.



\[2026-09-15 (approx, pre-log)\] engine/core/standard\_font.py, engine/core/resources.py, engine/core/config.py, [main.py](http://main.py) :: replaced custom SharpFont baked-atlas font system with a thin wrapper around arcade's built-in text drawing; fixed DPI/scaling via pyglet.options.dpi\_scaling = "real"; fixed the draw\_text PerformanceWarning across all files by pooling keyed arcade.Text objects in StandardFont

\[2026-09-15 (approx, pre-log)\] engine/core/display\_settings.py, [main.py](http://main.py), engine/views/editor\_view.py :: added monitor selection — window starts centered on primary/last-chosen monitor, SETTINGS > DISPLAY MONITOR cycles + saves choice to display\_settings.json

\[2026-09-15 (approx, pre-log)\] engine/views/editor\_view.py, editor\_grid.py, editor\_menu.py, editor\_overlays.py :: split monolithic editor\_view.py into grid drawing / top menu bar (TopMenuBar) / collision overlays, per project's no-monolithic-files rule

\[2026-09-15 (approx, pre-log)\] claude\_notes.md, project.md :: created claude\_notes.md as the up-to-date directory/file map; refreshed project.md into a bare file tree pointing at claude\_notes.md

\[2026-09-16 09:38\] engine/views/editor\_timeline.py :: new TimelineBar — Play/Pause/Reset, Continuous checkbox, draggable End-loop marker; snapshots every pymunk body's position/velocity/angle/spin on Play-from-stop, restores on Reset or End-marker hit

\[2026-09-16 09:38\] engine/views/editor\_view.py :: physics stepping moved from unconditional on\_update() call into timeline.update(); added throwaway TEMPORARY drifting/spinning test ball to prove the timeline mechanism before real physics nodes exist

\[2026-09-16 09:54\] [CHANGELOG.md](http://CHANGELOG.md) :: created — timecoded, structured, append-only log kept updated going forward with each change

\[2026-09-16 13:00\] engine/nodes/sockets.py, engine/nodes/base\_node.py :: added CONTROLLER data type and CONTROLLER node category (mint green)

\[2026-09-16 13:00\] engine/nodes/controls.py :: added Dropdown control (click-to-open list picker) alongside existing TextInput

\[2026-09-16 13:00\] engine/nodes/graph.py :: BUGFIX — NodeGraph.on\_mouse\_press never called a node's own on\_mouse\_press(px,py,button); this meant ImageImportNode's BROWSE button and ImageToCollisionNode's mode/detail buttons were silently non-functional (dead code, present since those nodes were built). Now calls it when a node defines one, before the generic drag-select check.

\[2026-09-16 13:00\] engine/nodes/library/object\_controller\_node.py :: new ObjectControllerNode (CONTROLLER category) — outputs a controller data packet (rotate\_left/right, accel\_forward/backward, shoot, afterburner, dock, activate) each frame; SOURCE dropdown: PLAYER (reads input\_state — WASD rotate/thrust, Shift afterburner, F dock, G activate, shoot unbound), NPC/CLAUDE (idle placeholders, no driving logic yet). No input sockets.

\[2026-09-16 13:00\] engine/nodes/sidebar.py :: registered Object Controller in the node palette

\[2026-09-16 13:00\] engine/core/input\_state.py :: new shared singleton — tracks held keys + F2 mute switch

\[2026-09-16 13:00\] engine/views/editor\_view.py :: F2 toggles input\_state mute (clears held keys on mute); on\_key\_press/release feed input\_state; added "INPUT: LIVE / MUTED (F2)" indicator top-right

\[2026-09-16 14:10\] engine/nodes/library/image\_to\_collision\_node.py, engine/nodes/library/image\_import\_node.py :: BUGFIX (crash) — on\_input\_received() took a second "value" arg that the graph never passes, crashing on connect/update; both files also had a broken propagate() referencing nonexistent wire.in\_socket/out\_socket. Root cause was hidden by the on\_mouse\_press dead-code bug (fixed earlier) which meant BROWSE had never actually loaded an image before. Fixed to match the RelayNode/ObjectController convention: on\_input\_received(self, socket) reads socket.value, outputs are set directly (out\_image.value / out\_collision.value), propagate() removed on both nodes.

  
aannd.

\[2026-10-17 UTC\] engine/nodes/wire\_visuals.py, engine/nodes/library/part\_placement\_node.py :: socket hover tooltip now names the socket as well as its type (WORLD - Image, HUD - Image, SHOP - Image ...) for every node; removed the labels drawn beside Part Placement's sockets (they overlapped its controls)



\[2026-10-17 UTC\] engine/parts/hull\_area.py, engine/parts/room\_grid.py :: room grid is centred on the hull picture (symmetric ship -> symmetric grid) and its edge padding is measured round instead of square, so slanted edges like the nose keep more cubes. Padding depth unchanged (1 cell). Tests extended

\[2026-10-17 UTC\] engine/parts/room\_grid.py, hull\_area.py, hull\_layout.py, engine/nodes/library/hull\_base.py, engine/views/internal\_view\_overlay.py :: HULL THICKNESS box on hull nodes (blank = auto, 6% of ship size in half cells, max 1); room grid auto-fits (slides under one cell for most cubes, symmetric tie-break); cells clipping outside the picture are dropped; buffer\_cells renamed thickness\_cells

\[2026-10-17 UTC\] engine/nodes/library/hull\_base.py :: thickness box label now says CELLS and sits closer to SUB HULL SLOTS so it fits the panel

  
thats claudes log of changes and notes based on what ive prompted, things we discussed and such. 

but I do have an intention to show how I go about beginning the process of making a program using claude at some point soon.  I do tutorial vids on youtube so its within my purview lol.

replies.author: Ferniclestix
replies.body:
https://i.redd.it/86xmtbe5g50i1.png

ill add this tho, consider giving claude tis own cookie jar,  it can be used to bypass some of its creativity restrictions when asking for unique ideas. i can ask mine to eat a cookie to maximise its inventiveness :)  we also trade cookies when it really likes an idea.

replies.author: clydeagain
replies.body: This is very cute and another impressive idea and usage but not convinced that eating a cookie will let claude be better than the model you've already set it to; I assume this is just for fun?

replies.author: Ferniclestix
replies.body:
To an extent.   
because its basiclally an averages type llm model, if I put it in a state using prompts where the AI is using patterns that on basis lead to more creative outputs   then it is put in that 'mindspace' of its ok to be a little more inventive.

using cookies I create a shared value system with scores. claude can independantly question the cookie jar to see how it earned cookies and how many it has to judge whether it wants to spend one based on its own outputs.

this puts claude in that mindspace of, this thing is worth something. 

so if i ask it to eat a cookie and come upt with something more inventive it does actually have those weights applied.

is it more effective than threatening it. saying oh please help ill be fired if this doesnt work  or whatever... i dont know. i know it ads a little bit tho, jusst a little.

plus, even tho i am likely anthromorphising it, I feel more comfortable that I can offer my AI an incentive for good work rather than midless praise.

just how I think.  
it was a fun little project, i like it :)

replies.author: clydeagain
replies.body: I do as well! Regardless if it works or not, what a refreshing and human idea lol
